title: The Internet Named a Ship Boaty McBoatface #shorts

lines.text: Britain asked the internet to name a 300-million-dollar research ship, and the internet screamed: Boaty McBoatface!
It won with over 124,000 votes, more than ten times what Sir David Attenborough's name got.
The government panicked, and named the ship after Attenborough instead.
But Boaty got revenge: the name went to a tiny submarine, which went exploring under Antarctica.
Moral: never let the internet name anything.

sources: https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2016/05/06/477010650/boaty-by-another-name-sir-david-attenborough-is-chosen-for-british-research-ship (NERC online poll; Boaty McBoatface >124,000 votes, over ten times the ~11,000 for Attenborough's name; ship ~$300M; science minister Jo Johnson chose RRS Sir David Attenborough; Boaty name given to a remotely operated sub-sea vehicle carried by the ship)

https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/boaty-mcboatface-completes-its-first-mission-180963863/ and https://noc.ac.uk/news/autosub-long-range-boaty-mcboatface-returns-home-after-successful-antarctic-mission (Boaty sub completed Antarctic missions in 2017)

facts.hedge: 'tiny submarine' = autonomous sub; cost rounded to 300 million dollars per NPR
